Hi Samir — Karthik from integrations here. Thanks for the details. A few notes from our side after a quick pass:

1) Token handling: the invite URL uses a single query parameter named "token" whose value is a URL-safe base64 string. Our validation code extracts the token parameter value and base64-decodes it. In general additional query params should be tolerated — we explicitly parse the querystring and pick "token".

2) Failure modes we've seen:
   - HTML email pipelines that rewrite links sometimes escape ampersands (& -> &) which can break downstream decoding in some clients.
   - Tracking proxies or redirectors that truncate the querystring after a certain length (tokens can be long).
   - Some web clients strip everything after a second question mark if the original link was embedded poorly.

To help us reproduce, can you paste one of the full invite URLs (exact as the recipient received it)? If you prefer, paste it into the attached sample-invite-link.txt (sanitized) and send that back. Also if you can tell us the mail client/version that observed the error, that helps.

Temporary workarounds you can try immediately:
- From the Redwood admin console we can resend the invite with tracking disabled — that will produce a link without extra UTM params.
- The invite token can be pasted directly into the portal in the "Enter invite token" box (if recipients are comfortable doing that).

We'll also add a short-term check on our redirect layer to be more tolerant of escaped ampersands and stray params if we see this at scale.

Attaching: sample-invite-link.txt (please paste the exact URL into the file and return)

Thanks,
